story: Japan went through five prime ministers in five years, each weaker than the last, while the long-ruling Liberal Democratic Party lost its majority in 2024 amid a slush-fund scandal. Then in October 2025 the party chose Sanae Takaichi, a hard-line conservative who admires Margaret Thatcher, as Japan's first woman prime minister. Within weeks she said Japan could respond militarily if China attacked Taiwan, the most direct statement by any sitting Japanese leader. China was furious and hit back where it hurt: it told its citizens not to travel to Japan, restricted seafood imports and even took back Japan's last two pandas (AFP via Edition.mv).

Takaichi bet that voters would side with her. She called a snap election in the middle of winter, only the third February vote since the war, and on 8 February the LDP won 315 of 465 seats, a two-thirds supermajority on its own for the first time in its 70-year history (Stanford APARC). The victory gives her the numbers to push higher military spending, a $135 billion stimulus and tax cuts that have rattled bond markets worried about Japan's enormous debt, and possibly to revise the pacifist constitution. Analysts read the result as voters endorsing her stand against Beijing's pressure. Japan has gone from a revolving door to one of the strongest governments among the rich democracies, led by a nationalist.
briefing.power: A constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system. The emperor is symbolic; the prime minister is chosen by the Diet, mainly the 465-seat House of Representatives, and leads the cabinet. The upper House of Councillors can delay legislation, and a two-thirds vote in both houses plus a referendum is needed to amend the constitution.
briefing.holders: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi (LDP), in office since October 2025.
